content.note: This file records which state deduction rules are implemented, the published year of each figure and what is left out. It is an evidence ledger, not a statement that any state's return is computed exactly. A `supported` state has its standard/itemized deduction, exemptions and federal income tax deduction (where the state allows one) computed from the sources below; other state adjustments and credits outside this module keep their existing treatment.

content: `table_year` is the tax year of the form or statute reproduced. For a later tax year, amounts flagged `indexed` are multiplied by the caller's state inflation factor (1.0 in 2026); unindexed statutory amounts never change. A tax year before `table_year` is not supported.
Federal income tax liability means regular tax plus AMT after nonrefundable credits. Each state then adds or removes specific Form 1040 items (`adds`/`subtracts`); see `FederalTaxComponents`.
All three implemented federal income tax deductions (AL, MO, OR) use the current-year liability (accrual) basis. None uses tax paid or refunds received.

State itemized deductions use raw categories. The IRC 164(b)(6)-(7) SALT cap (`federal_salt_cap`: $40,000 for 2025, $40,400 for 2026 rising 1% a year through 2029, reduced by 30% of income over $500,000 / $505,000, never below $10,000; halves for married filing separately) is applied only where the state adopts it, on the income measure the state names. Charitable limits are the IRC 170(b) 60% cash / 30% capital-gain-property shares.

content.note: Enacted later-year changes (`state_tax_enacted_changes.json`) alter two figures these rules own: the Hawaii (Act 46) and Virginia standard deductions. The rules apply them by year through `by_year` entries with the same amounts, and `tests/test_state_deduction_rules_coverage.py` checks that they match. The rules keep them at their nominal statutory amount; the enacted-changes path grows them with inflation after their year. Every other enacted change is to brackets, rates or retirement exclusions, which the rules do not own. Illinois' exemption sunset after 2028 is in its statute (35 ILCS 5/204(b)(7)) and is applied by the rules (`basic_last_tax_year`).

content: AL: the existing $3,000 standard deduction (doubled to $6,000 for joint returns) becomes the chart (for example $8,500 for a joint return with AL AGI below $26,000), exemptions are added and federal tax is deducted.
MO: the federal income tax deduction is added.
OR: 2026 indexed standard deduction, the federal tax subtraction and the exemption credit are added.
CT: the personal exemption, the 2% phase-out add-back, the recapture and the personal tax credit are added.
WI: the sliding standard deduction replaces the maximum, exemptions and the itemized deduction credit are added.

The spec-driven states replace the single built-in standard deduction (doubled for joint returns) with their own deduction, exemptions and credits. Notable corrections: Kentucky allows one standard deduction per joint return; Georgia, Oklahoma and Virginia follow the federal standard-or-itemized choice.

DC, Maine, Minnesota and New Mexico (added 2026-10-10) replace the built-in standard deduction with their own deductions, phase-outs and exemptions. DC and New Mexico follow the federal standard-or-itemized choice; Maine allows itemizing only to federal itemizers.
